| ` ` | LF-094 | tooling | risk | THEATRE SCALE 19. A grading policy that can press a button. THE LARGEST HOLE IN THE PROJECT. sim/engine.py never uses speed, call-wave, the kill chain, an ability, targeting priority or veterancy, so every one of the 24 anchor grades describes a player who uses none of them. That was an acceptable floor when sell() was the only unmodelled verb; it is not acceptable now that a third of the game is unmodelled, and scaling the board multiplies the gap rather than closing it<br><sub>Every balance number currently describes a player who never presses anything</sub> |
| ` ` | LF-105 | tooling | risk | PARITY BLIND SPOT: the gate never tests the build the owner plays. tools/test_parity.py goes through toolpaths.godot_argv(), and toolpaths.godot() prefers the native Linux build, so all 864 parity runs compare CPython against LINUX Godot. The owner plays the WINDOWS build. MEASURED across 100000 float64 samples on three runtimes: sqrt, fmod, +-*/, floor, round and manual hypot are byte-identical on all three, but Windows Godot (MSVC UCRT) diverges from CPython and Linux Godot (glibc) on atan2 0.084 percent, sin 0.133, cos 0.120, pow 0.130, log 0.031, exp 0.069 and tan 4.32 percent of samples. The rules currently use none of those ops so parity holds today BY ACCIDENT, not by design. Two fixes, both cheap: run test_parity.py against the Windows build at least once per release, and add a gate check that greps anchor_sim.gd and engine.py for the unsafe op set<br><sub>The build that ships is never compared against the reference</sub> |
| ` ` | LF-107 | design | risk | Free placement removes the denominator from the board saturation invariant. validate_data.py bounds capacity_mw against len(slots) x max_draw, and CLAUDE.md plus STATE.md both record this as a trap that already bit once: anchor-24 reached 103 percent of what would run every slot at maximum draw and the power decision the whole game is about had stopped existing on five levels. With no slots, board saturation is unbounded and the check has nothing to divide by. It must be re-derived from something else before free placement ships: a hard emplacement cap, buildable area divided by footprint area, or funds. This is the single biggest non-obvious cost of free placement and it attacks the core hook directly<br><sub>Free placement silently deletes the guard protecting the power economy</sub> |

| ` ` | LF-098 | engine | bug | An emplacement with nothing in range re-scans every unit on every tick, forever. anchor_sim.gd _step(): when target.is_empty() it does p.erase(aim); continue WITHOUT resetting cooldown, which has already gone <= 0 — so the next tick scans all U units again. Same in sim/engine.py. MEASURED: a board whose guns cover a currently empty lane costs 2.19x at 8 towers/32 units rising to 2.87x at 100/800 versus the same board with targets in range. This is exactly the shape a big multi-lane board produces, since most guns are idle most of the time. Fix must be mirrored in both engines and must not change WHICH unit is selected<br><sub>2.9x sim cost for guns that are doing nothing</sub> |
| ` ` | LF-106 | engine | risk | DECISION 030 IS PARTLY WRONG AND IT IS BLOCKING WORK. It says square roots are unsafe in the rules. MEASURED: IEEE-754 requires sqrt to be correctly rounded, both runtimes issue SQRTSD, and sqrt matched 100000 of 100000 samples across CPython, Linux Godot and Windows Godot. The actual culprit in decision 030 was Vector2.distance_to, a FLOAT32 helper: for 2 million points placed exactly on an integer radius, float32 and float64 disagree on the <= r test 10.2 percent of the time. So the rule to carry forward is float64 and never Vector2, NOT never sqrt. This matters because it unblocks off-grid geometry: continuous positions with sqrt-normalised directions ran 4000 ticks x 64 units bit-identical on all three runtimes. Supersede decision 030 with an entry that names the safe op set (+ - * / sqrt fmod floor min max comparisons) and the banned set (atan2 sin cos tan pow log exp, and anything through Vector2)<br><sub>A wrong rule is blocking a feature it was never about</sub> |
